Kozyatyn Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Vinnytska oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Kozyatyn grew rapidly after being founded as a railway station in 1874, its Jewish population swelling alongside the town's development; the 'Raid on Kozyatyn' saw Polish forces briefly capture the town during the Polish-Bolshevik War in April 1920. This cemetery, established in the second half of the 19th century, was demolished in 1953, with some of its tombstones later transferred to a new Jewish section within the town's Orthodox cemetery, documented elsewhere in this collection; a public park now occupies the former site.
